# Suyonandījātaka (Ja 360)
**ID:** Ja 360
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Suyonandījātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja360

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Suyonandījātaka* (also known as the *Sussondījātaka*, Ja 360) is a story in the canonical Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Cousins, Kunst, and Norman 1974]. In the framing story (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha relates the tale while staying at Jetavana to admonish a backsliding monk who regrets taking ordination due to the charms of a woman, observing that even ancient sages residing in the realm of the Garuḍas failed to protect themselves against womenfolk [SuttaCentral]. In the concluding identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the king of the past is identified as Ānanda and the Supaṇṇa king as the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1883]. In Burmese and other manuscript traditions recorded by Fausböll, the title appears as *Suyonandī* alongside the primary designation *Sussondījātaka* [Fausböll 1883].
Scholars note that the narrative shares its central theme with the *Kākāti Jātaka* (Ja 327), concerning the seduction or abduction of a king's principal wife by a supernatural being [Harris 2005]. Historically and geographically, the text is noteworthy for recording an early maritime voyage in which merchants of Bharukaccha (modern Broach) set sail across the sea for Suvaṇṇabhūmi [Cousins, Kunst, and Norman 1974].
No cross-language matches or curated non-Pali parallels are registered for this jātaka on SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse with the commentary in the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0513a3), sharing six matching passages comprising 883 characters, with the longest continuous correspondence spanning verses §2.1–5.4 [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§2.1–5.4 ↔ §1582–1596)
